title: Arignar Anna at the Bombay Conference: The Antiquity and Genius of Dravidian Linguistics (1961)
summary: In 1961 Bombay, C. N. Annadurai addressed an elite academic gathering on the linguistic independence and civilizational antiquity of the Dravidian language family.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 171: நேருவிடம் “அணிசேராத நாடுகள்” பட்டியல் கேட்கப்பட்டது
full_text:
In 1961, at a prestigious cultural and linguistic symposium held in Bombay, several prominent scholars asserted that all Indian vernaculars were derivative branches of Sanskrit, claiming that no independent linguistic family existed on the subcontinent.

C. N. Annadurai was invited to present the South Indian perspective. Stepping to the lectern before an audience of distinguished philologists and university vice-chancellors, Anna delivered an address of soaring scholarship:

"Distinguished scholars, I hold Sanskrit in high regard for its rich literature and ancient philosophical texts. But modern scholarship must be anchored in empirical linguistics, not chauvinistic mythology.

As established by pioneering philologists from Robert Caldwell to modern international linguists, the Dravidian family of languages is an entirely independent, primordial linguistic entity. It does not derive its syntactic structure, core vocabulary, or morphological foundation from Sanskrit!
Our foundational classical texts—from the ancient grammar of Tholkappiyam to the universal humanistic ethics of Thirukkural—flourished independently, reflecting an egalitarian civilizational ethos rooted in nature and civic fraternity. To insist upon linguistic uniformity is to misunderstand the very genius of India, which is an ancient garden of diverse and sovereign linguistic traditions!"

Anna’s erudite presentation was greeted with deep academic respect. He framed the Dravidian linguistic heritage not in parochial confrontation, but as a priceless treasure of world civilization.
